item.title: Splunk App for Secure Networking - v1.0.34 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Short Description:
Splunk App for Secure Networking provides configurable executive, IT operations, and secure-networking dashboards for Cisco environments, bringing network health, identity, security, infrastructure, application experience, building, and topology data into a unified Splunk experience.


Description:
Restricted Availability: This app is currently available only to approved users and is not yet generally available on Splunkbase. Broader availability is planned for a future release. Splunk App for Secure Networking helps organizations turn fragmented Cisco infrastructure, networking, identity, security, application-experience, and building telemetry into clear executive and operational insights within Splunk. Cisco environments often produce data across multiple products, add-ons, indexes, sourcetypes, and data models. Building a consolidated view normally requires teams to create and maintain separate searches, dashboards, index mappings, and visualizations. This app provides a reusable foundation that brings those signals together through configurable dashboards, shared search definitions, index-mapping macros, health indicators, drilldowns, and interactive topology views. The app includes Secure Networking Posture dashboards covering Zero Trust Access, Secure Infrastructure, Scalable Network Segmentation, Hybrid Mesh Firewalling, and Agentic Operations. It also provides executive briefing, IT health, security, asset inventory, network readiness, building intelligence, Cisco Spaces, and network-topology experiences. Searches use configurable index macros instead of hardcoded index names, allowing the app to adapt to different Splunk environments. Administrators can use the included Macro Index Tuning utility to discover relevant data and map the dashboards to their indexes. Splunk Executive Insights does not collect Cisco data directly. It visualizes data already ingested into Splunk through the applicable Cisco add-ons, integrations, and data models. The dashboards displayed and populated in each environment depend on the available data sources. The app is intended for network operations, security operations, IT operations, Splunk administrators, architects, customer-success teams, and executives who need a consolidated view of the health, security, availability, and performance of their Cisco environment.

item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
Version 2.1.0 is a compatibility and maintenance release for the Group-IB Threat Intelligence application for Splunk. It restores support for Splunk 9.x and completes the application's third-party license attribution.


Short Description:
Splunk application that ingests Group-IB Threat Intelligence feeds as structured events across 30+ collections. Search and correlate indicators against your own data, and risk-score and enrich IPs, domains, and hashes on demand with live Group-IB context.


Description:
Group-IB Threat Intelligence (TI) is a system for analyzing and attributing cyberattacks, threat hunting, and protecting network infrastructure based on data relating to adversary tactics, tools, and activity. Read more on the Group-IB website: https://www.group-ib.com/products/threat-intelligence. Threat Intelligence combines unique data sources and experience in investigating high-tech crimes and responding to complex multi-stage attacks worldwide. The system stores data on threat actors and related infrastructures collected since 2003, including those that criminals attempted to wipe out. This application integrates Group-IB Threat Intelligence with Splunk to consume TI feeds, run targeted detections, and pivot from a single indicator across all Group-IB collections. This Splunk integration allows you to: - Import and process Threat Intelligence feeds directly into Splunk as structured events, across 30+ Group-IB collections. - Search and correlate IoCs from Group-IB collections against your own data. - Score and enrich indicators (IP, domain, hash, URL) on demand with live Group-IB risk scores and threat context. - Run targeted detections and pivot from any indicator across all granted collections in real time. - Enrich internal alerts with external intelligence, and sync attacker infrastructure to Splunk Enterprise Security. To use this integration, you must have an active Group-IB Threat Intelligence license and API access. Need automated response actions? Pair this application with the Group-IB Threat Intelligence app for Splunk SOAR - https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/5968. The SOAR connector covers playbook-driven enrichment, case management, and bidirectional updates against the Group-IB portal.

## Supply Chain and AI Threat Intelligence Platform (SCIP) **Version 1.2.4 (build 246)** — Released 2026-08-03 ### Fixed - **Splunk Cloud Platform compatibility restored.** Updated an app configuration setting to maintain compatibility with new installs and upgrades on Splunk Cloud Platform. Existing Splunk Cloud Platform and Splunk Enterprise installations were not affected. - **Updated the bundled release notes file** to resolve a documentation-only issue identified during pre-release validation, prior to this release shipping. ### Improved - **MITRE ATLAS technique mapping updated across AI and agentic threat detections.** MITRE ATLAS is an evolving framework, and technique IDs, names, and tactic classifications are periodically revised as MITRE updates the standard. This release updates the AI/agentic threat detection library's technique IDs, names, and tactic classifications to align with current MITRE ATLAS data. Detections that address a real AI/agentic attack pattern but do not correspond to a technique currently defined in MITRE ATLAS are now clearly labeled as vendor-defined detections rather than presented under an ATLAS technique identifier. An automated consistency check now runs on every build to keep detection labels and the underlying ATLAS reference data in sync going forward.

Unifies software supply chain risk (SBOM/SCA), MITRE ATLAS AI-threat detection, and nine-framework compliance in one Splunk app — with FedRAMP-ready audit exports and no external security product required.

item.title: Adjutant AI (AI Workbench) - v2.1.0 [New App Release]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
# Adjutant AI (formerly AI Workbench) — Release notes What's new, improved, and fixed in each release, in plain language. This is the **customer-facing** summary used for the Splunkbase release-notes section; the full technical changelog lives in the project's detailed release notes. **Last updated:** 2026-07-29 > **About version numbers.** Releases once numbered 0.10–0.13 were renumbered to > 1.0–1.3 to reflect production maturity — no behaviour changed. The current release is > **2.1.0** — the **Fraud capability**, built on the **2.0 line** (the deterministic **ITSI Root > Cause Analysis** engine, **resource-consumption monitoring**, and **2.0.7**'s durable memory, > Scheduled Ask and governed integrations), which in turn built on > **1.8.5** (the **CIM Coverage Audit**), **1.8.4** (async playbook execution over MCP > plus the **Outcome Ledger** executive/audit dashboard), **1.8.3** > (a security‑hardening release: OWASP + dependency + anti‑ransomware audit), **1.8.2** (Splunk > Edge Processor data‑quality awareness and keyless Azure OpenAI authentication), **1.8.1** > (support‑diagnosis fixes) and **1.8.0** (agent telemetry & OCSF export, content packs, > all‑tiers data‑quality checks, Splunk 10.x readiness, Dashboard Studio version‑awareness). The > **1.7.0** ServiceNow integration and the **1.5.0 "Data Foundation & MCP OAuth"** themes are > included below. --- ## 2.1.0 "Fraud" Splunk's own App for Fraud Analytics reaches end of life on 1 May 2027, and it is not alone: the App for Anomaly Detection retired in 2025, standalone UBA ends in January 2027, and the App for Behavioral Profiling froze at Splunk 9.4. Four packaged analytics apps retiring on one path, and their customers have no answer today. This release is that answer. - **Find out what your data can actually support, in about a minute.** The Fraud Data Coverage Audit reads your real events and tells you which fraud use cases you can run today, which are partial and why, and which are blocked with the feed that is missing named. It works out which of your sources is which by looking at what they CONTAIN, not what they are called, because real sourcetypes never match the documentation. Today this answer takes a workshop and three weeks of a consultant. - **The check nobody else makes.** It measures whether your entity keys actually survive from one feed to the next. Ring detection is the payoff use case and it is the one most often declared ready on the strength of the fields being present, then failing because an account or device cannot be followed across the boundary. It also tells you when a feed carries every field perfectly but only knows about a fraction of your customers, which is a different problem with a different fix. - **Count actors, not accounts.** One person can open many accounts using the fact that Gmail ignores dots, and to your signup system they look like many different people. Adjutant knows to collapse those, and knows NOT to do it for other providers, where merging two customers would invent a fraud ring that does not exist. When it links entities it always shows you how rare the shared attribute is, because a shared IP address means nothing behind a mobile network and a great deal on a home line. - **Scoring that fits where you already are.** If you run Enterprise Security, everything goes into your existing risk framework and nothing parallel is built. If you do not, it uses the same field names anyway, so the day you buy ES you change a destination rather than rewrite your detections. - **Behavioural profiling that outlives the app it replaces.** Describe the behaviour in a sentence and get a working indicator, anomaly rule and ranked entity list. It compares an entity against its own history, or against its peer group, which the retiring app could not do. It also watches for a feed dying behind a profile: when that happens the scores simply fade, and fading looks exactly like everyone behaving better. - **Nothing here needs those retiring apps.** Every playbook, tool and piece of knowledge works on a plain Splunk estate. What we took from the retiring apps is their METHOD, not a dependency on them: the risk-contribution model, the behavioural profiling pattern, the entity pivots and the fraud use case catalogue are all reimplemented here and improved. If you do still run either app, importers can lift what you built into the native form, but that is a convenience rather than the point. - **The fraud patterns it now knows.** Signup fraud (many accounts sharing an email, IP, phone, password or bank account), account takeover (brute force against credential stuffing, one address against many accounts, impossible travel, and the profile-change-then-money-movement chain), money laundering (funds converging then dispersing, amounts kept just under a reporting threshold, sanctioned-country exposure), and two narrow verticals in unemployment-insurance claims and controlled-substance diversion. All of it reworded into our own framing, with nothing copied from Splunk's documentation. - **Eight playbooks**, including triage for both public sector claims and financial fraud. Both start by checking the data is actually flowing before offering any verdict, because a quiet fraud queue is either good news or a dead feed, and you should know which. Fraud features need Splunk Enterprise and the fraud licence feature. Where either is missing they stay visible and explain what is needed rather than disappearing. The demonstration dataset has no licence requirement at all, so a trial environment always works. One thing said plainly: Adjutant AI is not a fraud detection engine and does not try to be. It will not decline a card payment in a hundred milliseconds; that is what the dedicated engines are for. It is the layer above them that finds what they miss across channels, connects the entities they cannot, and turns three weeks of investigation into an afternoon with a trail you can hand to an auditor. ## 2.0.7 "Memory, Scheduled Ask & Integrations" Adjutant AI gains a durable memory, a scheduled/unattended surface, and a governed data-integration subsystem — so it stops re-asking, can run on a clock, and can sync a system of record into Splunk under a contract two humans have reviewed. - **Memory — it stops re-asking.** A small, durable, per-tenant memory: **learned facts** (the index a report uses, what "the Cribl search" means for a team) captured the moment they're learned, and **integration watermarks**. Two new Knowledge tabs — **Learned Knowledge** (a confirm queue; promote a fact to the whole Org) and **Integration State** (force a watermark to replay or skip). Unattended runs use **confirmed facts only**; a captured-but-unconfirmed fact can't silently steer a run that writes to a target. Backed up per Org with the daily KV Store backup; a content-pack upload never overwrites it. - **"Templates" are now "Playbooks."** A presentation rename that finishes an inconsistency the engine already had (the alert action was always "Run Investigation Playbook"). No data migration. Explicit **run-mode tags** (`triggered` / `scheduled` / `integration`) replace the old bare `playbook` tag. - **Scheduled Ask.** A new admin tab to run a Playbook on a cron schedule — a **Scheduled Job** (run and deliver a result; Professional+) or a **Scheduled Integration** (read a source, write a target, keep watermarks; `ai-integration` feature). Each is a private, service-account-owned saved search that just *triggers* a governed, single-flighted, bounded run — no per-member scheduler racing over shared state (the DB-Connect-on-search-head-cluster lesson applied). - **Governed integrations.** A **mapping spec** is the contract: a versioned, declarative, lint-checked `source → transforms → destination` record the runner executes deterministically — the model never transforms rows. Author it in the new **Mappings** tab (a visual three-pane pipeline editor with a live sample rail, or JSON), promote it **4-eyes**, and **earn** unattended clearance after a verified run. Schema **drift** is detected deterministically, diagnosed by the assistant, and decided by a human — never a silent rewrite. Records land via **`splunk_writer`** (KV Store / CSV / HEC / spool, per-record routing, a fail-closed destination allowlist from the contract). Two ServiceNow example mappings and a standard mapping-driven integration Playbook ship to clone and parameterize. See `docs/ADJUTANT_MEMORY_AND_SCHEDULED_ASK.md` for the operator guide. ## 2.0.6 "ITSI RCA — Industrialise" The Root Cause Analysis engine reaches its industrialise milestone, and the smaller items deferred from earlier trains are completed. All analysis-only and off by default. - **Recovery verification** — after RCA names a cause, re-check whether the service actually recovered (which corroborates the cause) or is still degraded / newly regressed elsewhere. - **Calibrated confidence** — where enough analyst feedback exists, the engine shows a genuinely calibrated likelihood for a candidate instead of a raw internal score; until then it keeps the existing strength wording (never a made-up number). - **Draft, recommend-only remediations** — RCA can produce reviewable draft fixes routed by cause (restore the feed on the culprit host, fix onboarding/timestamp config, restart a stalled input, correct the monitoring, look upstream, add a KPI). Always a suggestion — never executed. - **Data-driven playbook** — the RCA phase sequence is now a validated, dependency-checked contract rather than a hardcoded list (same order, now extensible). - **Sharper feed diagnosis** — names which forwarder/HEC/pipeline host is the culprit, and adds dedicated Cribl and Edge Processor pipeline-health checks. - **Better lineage & safety** — resolves raw host/IP to canonical ITSI entities via declared aliases; follows saved-search/eventtype references inside subsearches; and hardens the unattended template so it can only follow the unattended procedure. --- ## 2.0.5 "Resource-consumption monitoring" A clear, per-tenant answer to *"how much does Adjutant AI cost to run?"* - **New "Resource Consumption" dashboard** shows the CPU, memory, threads and Splunk search-slots Adjutant AI uses — broken down **by Org and by Org/Business-Unit** and by workload (interactive Ask, unattended RCA, unattended runs, and — soon — scheduled Asks). - **Real per-run measurements.** Unattended work runs in its own process, so the app now records actual CPU-seconds, peak memory and thread counts for each RCA cycle and each automation run, tagged with the Org/BU it ran for. The numbers are content-free (counters only) and always on. - **Honest by design.** Interactive Ask runs inside Splunk's shared handler, where memory can't be pinned to one tenant — so for Ask the dashboard reports search CPU/slots (from Splunk's own audit log, mapped to Org/BU) and token/cost usage, and says so plainly, instead of inventing a figure. Additive and safe; no change to how analyses behave. --- ## 2.0.4 "ITSI RCA — discovery & external fold-in" The ITSI Root Cause Analysis engine completes its discovery train: - **Latent-dependency discovery** surfaces a likely service dependency that isn't declared in your ITSI topology but shows up in the data (shared inputs/entities, at-the-same-moment degradation) — proposed as a ready-to-review suggestion, never created automatically. - **External-AI fold-in** can consult an external AI provider's read of the incident and weigh it in as corroborating evidence — it can strengthen or temper a finding, but never overrides the engine's own deterministic verdict. Analysis-only and off by default. --- ## 2.0.3 "ITSI RCA — data-supply legs" The ITSI Root Cause Analysis engine learns to read a KPI's **data supply chain as distinct legs**: - It classifies where a KPI's data actually comes from — a DB Connect input, a universal forwarder, HEC, an Edge Processor / Cribl pipeline, syslog, or a scripted input — and shows which leg carries the most data ("the largest bar"). - When a feed problem occurs, it can point at the **specific leg** that failed (for example "the DB Connect leg stalled") instead of just flagging the whole index. - Behaviour-drift baselines can now be **seasonal** (same time last week) as well as the 7-days-prior default, so normal weekly patterns aren't mistaken for problems. Analysis-only; changes nothing about how the engine behaves until you opt in. --- ## 2.0.2 "ITSI RCA — KPI Behaviour Analysis" The ITSI Root Cause Analysis engine learns to read **how your KPIs are behaving**, not just whether they are red: - **Every KPI, including healthy ones, is profiled for behaviour drift** — a meaningful shift in a KPI's value that its own red/green threshold may miss (for example, response time slowly creeping up after debug logging was accidentally left on). - **Entity-level behaviour** pinpoints *which* entities are driving a service's degradation, not just that the service is unhealthy. - **Suggested-KPI recommendations**: where the analysis finds a blind spot the current KPIs don't measure, it proposes a monitoring improvement — always a suggestion, never a root-cause claim. All of this is analysis-only and off by default; it changes nothing about how the engine behaves until you opt in. --- ## 2.0.1 "Unattended engine hardening" The unattended investigation engine (the part of Adjutant AI that can investigate an alert with no human watching) is designed to hand the alert back to Splunk immediately and do the work in the background. That is what keeps your alerts fast — but it also means nobody is watching if a background run misbehaves. This release makes sure a misbehaving run always stops, and that you can see it when one does. The engine still ships **switched off**. If you have never enabled it, nothing changes for you. **Fixed** - **A run that keeps failing now gives up instead of restarting forever.** If a background run died, it was put back in the queue and started again — without counting how many times it had already failed. A run that failed every time (a bad playbook, a bug) could restart indefinitely and keep occupying a worker. Runs are now retried a set number of times and then parked as "given up", where they stop consuming anything and wait for a person. - **The per-run time limit now actually applies.** The "maximum time for one run" setting was shown in the configuration, charted on the dashboard and alerted on — but nothing enforced it. Runs now stop when they reach it. - **A stuck run is stopped, not just forgotten.** Previously the engine handed the work to a new run but left the stuck one alive, so two runs could work on the same alert and both spend money. The stuck one is now stopped first. - **Long, healthy runs are no longer interrupted.** A slow-but-fine run could be mistaken for a dead one and restarted underneath itself. Runs now report that they are alive continuously rather than only between steps. **New** - **Limits that protect Splunk itself.** A background run now caps its own memory, CPU and priority, so a runaway run degrades into one failed investigation instead of putting the Splunk platform under pressure. Sensible defaults are set for you; all are adjustable, and each can be switched off. - **You can now see stuck and given-up runs.** A run only reports on itself when it finishes, so runs that got stuck were invisible on every dashboard. The *Pipeline Knobs* dashboard has a new run-health section (stuck runs, given-up runs, runs being retried, and what each worker is doing), and two new optional alerts — **Runner stuck** and **Runs dead-lettered** — tell you without anyone having to look. Both are off by default. **Changed** - The retry setting is now called **`runner_max_attempts`** (it covers every kind of failure, not only runaway runs). The unused `retain_completed_hours` setting has been removed — run history retention is controlled by `queue_retention`. If you set either in a local override, update it. --- ## 1.8.5 "CIM Coverage Audit" When a data source is onboarded but a correlation search in Enterprise Security still comes back empty, or an ITSI KPI never fills, the cause is almost always that the source is not properly mapped to the CIM data model the search depends on. Finding out why is normally a slow, manual walk through the layers. The CIM Coverage Audit does it for you, from your real events and your real search head configuration. **New** - **Audit a sourcetype against a CIM dataset.** Ask, for example, audit cisco:asa against the Network Traffic All_Traffic dataset. You get back how much of the dataset the source covers, and if it does not, which layer is broken: the source is not tagged so the model cannot see it, its index is not on the model's allowlist, a field is missing or under the wrong name, a value needs normalizing, or the accelerated summaries the correlation searches read have not caught up. That last one is the confusing case where CIM works when you test it by hand but your correlation searches fire nothing, and the audit calls it out plainly. - **A fix you can read and deploy.** For each gap the audit produces the exact configuration, checked for validity, shown as your current stanza next to the proposed one, with a note on where it belongs. It never deploys anything itself. You review and apply it, which is what lets you run this where an automatic write to production would never pass change control. - **Honest about what a search head can see.** Adjutant AI runs on the search head, so it reads your search time configuration and the real events, and it is upfront that it cannot read the index time configuration on your indexers. It runs its searches as you, so it can never read data from an index you could not otherwise search. - Three read only helpers to read a sourcetype's search head props and transforms and check where a sourcetype has data. The diagnosis is available on Professional so any platform team can see which layer is broken. Generating the validated fix is an Enterprise feature. It grades against the CIM add on actually installed on your search head. Restart Splunk after upgrading. **Fixed** - **The app opens on the Ask tab again.** If your LLM runs entirely on the search head, with the key held server side (the Splunk proxy mode, an Azure managed identity, or a Bedrock role), the browser never receives an API key. The app used to read that as nothing being configured and jumped to the Settings tab on every launch. It now opens on Ask as intended, and only sends you to Settings when a key really is needed and missing. - **Clearer license status.** When a license is installed but the app cannot confirm it is active on this environment, it now tells you that directly instead of quietly dropping to the free Personal tier. Admins get a pointer to the License page to re-activate. --- ## 1.8.4 "Async playbooks over MCP" Run Adjutant AI playbooks from an AI agent over the Model Context Protocol with a reliable **start → poll → fetch** pattern. A playbook can take several minutes, but AI tool calls are subject to short timeouts you don't control (the MCP server, the client, proxies), so trying to wait for the answer in one call is fragile. Now every call returns in seconds. **New / Improved** - **Start returns immediately.** `adjutantai_start_playbook` (the old `adjutantai_run_playbook` name is removed) hands back a run id at once with a hint on how to poll. - **Check progress** with `adjutantai_get_playbook_status` — queued, running, completed, or failed (a run that hit a recoverable error and is auto‑retrying is reported as still running, not failed), with guidance to stop polling after ~15 minutes. - **Fetch the verdict** with `adjutantai_get_playbook_results` once completed — condensed by default, or the full result on request; a partial result is clearly labelled. - **Tenant‑safe.** One team can't read another team's run; unknown or expired run ids simply return "not found." Run records are kept for 7 days by default. - **Try it out of the box:** start `MCP Example: Read-only Health Check` under Org/BU `DFLT/DFLT` (the read‑only reference playbook shipped on every install), then poll and fetch. Requires the inbound MCP server and the Backend Ask Service to be enabled. No configuration changes. Restart Splunk after upgrading. ### Also in 1.8.4 — the Outcome Ledger (Enterprise) A single screen that answers what a CEO, CISO or auditor actually asks: *what did agentic AI do for us this period, was it any good, what did it save, what did it cost — and can I see the evidence for one run?* It assembles data the app already records (unattended‑run history, analyst agreement, run telemetry, LLM spend) into one executive/audit view. It adds **no new data collection and sends nothing to any external service.** **New** - **The dashboard** (`Adjutant AI ▸ Outcome Ledger`): headline tiles (investigations run without a human, how often analysts agreed with the AI — with the sample size and coverage shown, benign/false‑positive runs auto‑closed, analyst hours saved, LLM spend, typical time to a verdict), the mix of AI conclusions over time, agreement by case type, a weekly ledger, and an **evidence** table you can click through to the full detail of any single run. A footer spells out every assumption so a number is never quoted out of context. - **Safe to hand to an auditor.** What each viewer may see is decided on the server from their own identity — never from the page — and fails closed. In this release the dashboard is for Splunk administrators; scoped, delegated auditor access is the next step. - **Is the AI real, or just performing?** An Efficacy Trend panel puts run volume against how often analysts agreed, over time. If the agent runs more while analysts increasingly override it, the panel says so ("scaling faster than trust") instead of hiding it behind a healthy‑looking headline — and on too little feedback it honestly says the sample is too thin to judge. - **Honest numbers.** Effort saved is shown as time (with the per‑case assumption stated), spend is the real logged cost, and the per‑investigation efficiency signal is token usage — never an invented cost estimate. Enterprise feature. No effect on any existing behaviour. Restart Splunk after upgrading. --- ## 1.8.3 "Security hardening" A security‑focused release. Adjutant AI was put through an independent OWASP Top 10 (web **and** LLM), dependency‑vulnerability, and "AI‑driven ransomware" review. The headline: **no critical issues, no default passwords or keys, no vulnerable components that ship to you, and the assistant cannot be turned into an attack tool.** Confirmed issues are fixed; a plain‑language, reviewer‑ready write‑up ships in the app as `SECURITY_AUDIT.md`. **Improved / Fixed** - **Credentials stay server‑side.** Provider API keys and keyless Azure sign‑in secrets are never sent to the browser or to other users in your tenant. (The free‑tier browser API‑key path is unchanged.) - **Prompts stay in your audit index**, not Splunk's internal logs. - **Stronger multi‑tenant isolation** for investigation results and knowledge sources. - **You confirm every change.** Closing a notable, setting a disposition, an ITSI/TrackMe/ServiceNow write, or overwriting a saved dashboard now asks for explicit confirmation first. Read‑only questions and new private dashboards are unaffected. - **General hardening:** cleaner errors, tighter sign‑in redirects, safer content‑pack imports, email TLS verification on by default. No new features or config changes. Restart Splunk after upgrading. --- ## 1.8.2 "Edge Processor data-quality + keyless Azure OpenAI auth" **Keyless Azure OpenAI (Microsoft Entra ID / managed identity).** Connect Azure OpenAI **without a static API key** — using a Microsoft Entra ID service principal or a managed identity, governed by your Entra tenant. Runs entirely server-side (no token reaches the browser), supports Public and US Gov clouds, and adds a one-click **Test connection** that names exactly what to fix if something is off. Connecting Azure with a plain **API key** still works on every tier; the keyless Entra path is an **Enterprise** capability. --- ### Edge Processor data-quality If your data passes through **Splunk Edge Processor** before it reaches Splunk, some parsing, timestamping, dropping and routing happens *upstream* — where Splunk's own internal logs and feed-health tools can't see it. This release teaches the assistant to look at that hop. - **New "Edge Processor → Splunk data-quality check".** Ask the assistant to check an Edge Processor feed and it reads Edge Processor's own operational metrics (throughput, dropped events, failed destination sends, and queue backpressure) and tells you, in plain language, whether data is being silently lost or delayed before it lands — with a proof dashboard. - **Honest by design.** If Edge Processor telemetry isn't reaching your Splunk yet, the assistant says so and gives you the exact setup steps (on-premises vs Splunk Cloud) instead of inventing a clean bill of health. It reports at the pipeline level and is clear that per-event checks need a small addition to your Edge Processor pipeline. - **Folds into the readiness verdict.** Edge Processor joins Splunk parsing, feed-health, and Cribl as another "is this data actually good?" signal, and can cap the Data Quality Score when it finds upstream loss. - Read-only and available on every tier, exactly like the existing Cribl check. --- ## 1.8.1 "Cleaner support diagnosis" A small maintenance update over 1.8.0 (front-end only). - **More accurate "Report an issue" diagnosis.** The automated issue classifier no longer mislabels a session that finished normally — one that completed and produced its dashboard — as having "run out of tool steps." The suspected-issue summary in your support bundle is now cleaner for healthy, tool-heavy sessions. --- ## 1.8.0 "Agent telemetry & OCSF export, content packs & all-tiers data quality" **New — your SOC can watch the agent (OCSF telemetry).** - **Adjutant AI emits its own activity as OCSF.** Every LLM call, tool / MCP / ServiceNow call, configuration change, unattended run verdict, and **policy refusal** (the proof the controls actually fire) can be written as open-standard **OCSF** events to a Splunk index your Enterprise Security / SOC already watches — mapped to CIM via the community **OCSF-CIM Add-On**. Your SOC monitors our agent the same way it monitors everything else: on-prem, with no cloud egress. - **You stay in control.** It is **off by default** and Enterprise-gated. **You provision and name the index** (the app ships no `indexes.conf`). Routing and content are resolved **per Organisation / Business Unit**; content export is denied by default and never exceeds your audit (DPIA) ceiling, with a server-side redaction check before anything is written. - **See it immediately.** A shipped admin dashboard — *Adjutant AI — Behaviour (OCSF)* — shows the token trend, model mix, tool/MCP egress with identity, the refusal and finding feeds, and a per-run drilldown, all on raw OCSF (no CIM Add-On required). **New — update Adjutant's content without waiting for a whole new app release.** - **Content packs.** Almost everything Adjutant does well lives in its **content** — the skills, knowledge, and playbooks. A **content pack** is a single, versioned file that lets us ship a corrected or improved content set straight to your install, and lets your admin apply it safely — no Splunkbase re-vetting cycle for a content fix. - **Your changes are protected.** Applying a pack **upgrades only the items you haven't changed**. Anything your team has customised is left exactly as-is and clearly listed, never silently overwritten — and your Org/BU scoping is always preserved. After an import you get a per-item report, and the list of items that need manual reconciliation is downloadable as a CSV. - **Safe by design.** Every pack carries an integrity check, so a tampered or truncated file is refused. Imports live on the **Backups** page, which also shows which content version you're currently on — run a backup first and you can roll back in one click. - **Retire without deleting.** A pack can mark an item **retired** — it stays installed but is hidden and switched off everywhere (it can't be picked, run, or used by the assistant). An admin can re-enable it at any time by removing the tag. **Improved — data-quality checks for everyone, and Splunk 10.x readiness.** - **Data-quality ingestion checks are now available on every edition, including the free tier.** Checking whether a feed is actually landing and parsing correctly — on `index=_internal`, through **TrackMe**, and through **Cribl Stream** — is a baseline capability now, not a Professional add-on. - **Ready for Splunk Enterprise 10.2 and 10.4.** The app declares Python 3.9 **and** 3.13 compatibility and has been audited against the 10.x platform changes (dashboards, the web framework, KV Store). Your admin still completes the standard KV Store engine migration as part of any 10.x upgrade. - **Smarter Dashboard Studio building.** The assistant now works from a single, version-aware map of what Dashboard Studio supports on **your** Splunk version — it won't reach for a chart type your version can't render, and when your Splunk is newer than what we've documented it builds conservatively and verifies the result. **Fixed.** - **Fewer false "the dashboard is blank" errors.** A heavy Dashboard Studio dashboard that renders fine but slowly is no longer wrongly reported as blank — the assistant confirms the panels actually returned data before deciding, so it stops wasting a retry on a dashboard that was already correct. A genuinely blank dashboard is still caught. - **TrackMe panels only when they belong.** Fixed a rule that pushed a TrackMe feed-health panel onto every generated dashboard (and used a lookup that fails outside the TrackMe app). The assistant now adds a feed-health panel only when it's actually relevant, using a method that works in your app. --- ## 1.7.0 "ServiceNow integration" (included in the 1.8.0 release) > **Renamed to Adjutant AI.** The app is now **Adjutant AI** (formerly "AI Workbench"). > This is a **display-name change only** — the in-app title (the easter egg now lives on > the dot of the "i" in **Adjutant Ai**), the app label, the documentation, and the > assistant's own self-description all say **Adjutant AI**. Nothing functional changed: > the Splunk app id, your saved searches/dashboards/models, KVStore data, and generated > artifact names are unchanged, so the upgrade is seamless. **New — run playbooks automatically, and from other Splunk apps.** - **On a schedule or on an event.** A playbook can run **unattended** on a schedule (a "morning health check") or in response to a Splunk event — an alert, an ES correlation search, or an ITSI episode. When an event triggers it, the affected thing (the host, user, or entity in the alert) is handed to the playbook automatically, so it investigates exactly what fired. Two ready-made (disabled) examples are included to copy. - **Adjutant AI as a building block for other apps.** Other Splunk AI agents can now ask Adjutant AI to **list** and **run** your playbooks through a small, safe interface (an MCP server). Only playbooks you mark **MCPready** are exposed, every call must name the Org/BU it is for (which must be a business unit you have set up) as a safeguard, and runs go through the same governed, bounded service — never an open door. This interface is **off by default** — turn it on with one setting. When on, the tools can also appear inside **Splunk's own MCP Server**, reachable on the normal Splunk web address (no special port needed); you authenticate with a standard Splunk token. A ready-made, read-only **example playbook** ships enabled so there is always something to see the moment you switch the interface on. **New — "Report an issue" support packaging (all editions).** - One click on any conversation (per-turn 🐞, the Ask panel, or the new **Help tab**) packages exactly what happened — versions, the resolved prompt, the tools and model used, the generated dashboards/searches, and every error and warning — into a single file. - **Safe by construction:** secrets are stripped before anything leaves the browser, and the file is **encrypted** to the support key, so it's safe to send over any channel. - It even **tells you what kind of problem it looks like** and matches known issues, so simple cases are solved without a back-and-forth. - **Send it your way:** download it and attach it to your own ticket, use the built-in support form, or email it. The **Help tab** (Report + Documentation + About) is always reachable — even if the app is locked by licensing. **New — ServiceNow, done properly** (Professional + the `servicenow` feature). Read incidents, changes, problems and the **CMDB/CSDM** in plain English — with bounded blast-radius / dependency traversals ("what's the blast radius if this CI fails?"). Turn a Splunk alert, ITSI episode or ES notable into a rich, deterministically rendered ServiceNow incident and **write the number back** to the originating object (a re-fire updates, never duplicates; the closed-incident policy is configurable). **Security incidents (SIR)** with MITRE ATT&CK, off until an admin enables them. Two transports (REST **or** a ServiceNow MCP server), plus TISC threat-intel enrichment — all server-side and allowlisted, so ServiceNow can never block the assistant. *(Verified against the documented APIs and unit-tested; final certification is on a live ServiceNow.)* **New — run playbooks automatically, and from other apps.** Playbooks can run **unattended** on a schedule, or from a Splunk alert / ES correlation search / ITSI episode (the triggering entity is handed to the run). Adjutant AI can also expose **list / run** over an inbound **MCP server** (off by default, MCPready-only, Org/BU-scoped) — reachable inside Splunk's own MCP Server on the normal web address, with a standard Splunk token. **New — "Report an issue" support packaging (all editions).** One click packages a failing conversation — secret-stripped and **encrypted client-side** — with an automatic problem classification, plus an always-reachable **Help tab** even when the app is licence-locked. **New — Cribl Stream data-quality awareness** (Professional+). Reads Cribl's own forwarded logs and metrics to surface the timestamp / parse / dropped-event problems that happen *inside Cribl, before Splunk can see them* — the "green in Splunk but timestamped wrong" blind spot — folded into one readiness verdict. No Cribl Lake or Search required. **New — LLM reliability: retry, fallback & circuit breaker** (Enterprise). A brief provider hiccup (503 / 529 / rate-limit) auto-retries within a time budget; a per-config **circuit breaker** stops hammering a provider that's down, then probes for recovery; and an ordered **fallback** transparently switches to your next provider (and tells you which it used). Two new admin dashboards — **LLM Health** and **AI Activity** — plus per-user / BU / org concurrency caps, all conservative and off the critical path. **New — live model & cost catalogue (all editions).** Models and prices come from a runtime catalogue that updates without an app rebuild; **automatic model discovery** (Professional+) keeps it current without ever logging your keys; an Enterprise admin screen adds price overrides and manual model registration for private gateways. **Fixed.** Generated Simple XML dashboards now share a single base search across panels (faster) and get a top data-ingestion health panel; corrected a 3× Opus price over-charge (now server-side authoritative, with Opus 4.8 and Fable 5 included). --- ## 1.5.0 "Data Foundation & MCP OAuth" **New:** connect to **OAuth 2.1‑protected MCP servers** (authorization‑code + PKCE for interactive, client‑credentials for unattended; tokens held server‑side, never in the browser — see [MCP_OAUTH.md](MCP_OAUTH.md)); **onboard new data sources** — describe a source or attach a sample file and get a deployment‑ready add‑on package; a **"is my data parsed correctly?"** ingestion/timestamp check that reads Splunk's own internal logs; generated config **validated against your instance** and given a **0–100 Data Quality Score** (A–F); and attach a local sample file in Ask (only the file name is audited, never contents). **Improved:** works with the newest OpenAI "reasoning" models incl. Azure GPT‑5.4 / GPT‑5.4‑mini (auto‑detects the request format); more reliable generated dashboards; generated objects use the **`aiworkbench`** name tag; and Audit‑tab improvements (Business Unit column/filter, local‑timezone timestamps, reliable token/outcome capture). --- ## Earlier releases (1.0.0 – 1.4.3) - **1.4.3** — Clearer guidance and plain-language fixes when a free-tier LLM key hits its provider limits (e.g. Groq token-per-minute caps, Gemini zero-quota keys); the LLM config screen flags these up front. - **1.4.1** — Per-feature capability licensing with edition badges (Professional / Enterprise / MSP); gated features show a padlock, and nothing you created is ever deleted when a tier changes. Turn-level audit logging made reliable; more robust dashboard generation. - **1.4.0** — The assistant reads your own Splunk **live** (real search commands + installed visualizations) instead of guessing; Splunk Security Essentials detection content integrated. - **1.3.3** — TrackMe integration end-to-end (feed-health awareness + actions) with richer built-in platform knowledge. - **1.3.2** — First Splunkbase 1.x release: packaging and permissions hardening. - **1.3.1** — Fixed Org/BU edits dropping fields; safeguard to keep bundled playbooks correct after upgrades. - **1.3.0** — Real, per-Organisation audit logging of every AI interaction (Professional+). - **1.2.0** — Splunk Security Essentials content tools for playbooks. - **1.1.1** — Cisco Deep Time Series Model (CDTSM) playbooks: pre-trained anomaly detection and forecasting via the AI Toolkit, each with a proof dashboard. - **1.1.0** — Multi-tenancy and the Organisation / Business-Unit editor overhauled for clearer, safer tenant scoping. - **1.0.0** — The knowledge layer: ground answers in your organisation's own conventions. *(Releases before 1.0 are early pre-release history and are omitted here.)* --- ## Known issues - **Open the assistant from inside another app.** Adjutant AI is a "host shell": reach it from a navigation-menu entry inside Search, Enterprise Security, ITSI, or your own apps — not by clicking the app tile directly. Everything it creates lands in the namespace of the app you opened it from. - **Some Data Foundation features need self-hosted Splunk.** The configuration-reference grounding and config-package generation (1.5.0) read files on the Splunk server, so they are unavailable on Splunk Cloud; the assistant says so and continues with what it can. --- *When a published fix resolves a tracked GitHub issue, it is summarised here with its issue number — for example: "Fixed: a dashboard panel could display raw HTML markup as text instead of formatting it (#123)."*


Short Description:
A workbench for Splunk, not just a chatbot. Analyse, correlate and build across SPL, dashboards, alerts, AI Toolkit / MLTK, ES, ITSI and TrackMe through tools that understand each one — plus any MCP server you add. Pick your LLM: Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure, Groq, Gemini, Bedrock, Ollama, OpenRouter. Multi-tenant, multi-tier (Free, Pro, Enterprise, MSP).


Description:
Adjutant AI (formerly AI Workbench) is a generative workspace for Splunk — not a chatbot bolted onto search, but a real workbench where you investigate, analyse and build with tools that understand Splunk. It is a host shell: it has no use-cases of its own, deriving everything from the Splunk app a user opens it from and their roles. Install once on the Search Head, then embed it in the apps your users already live in — Search, ITSI, Enterprise Security, your SOC and MSP customer apps. Users never leave the app they came from, and artefacts land in that app's namespace. Ask in plain English. Get back validated SPL, Simple XML and Dashboard Studio dashboards, alerts, lookups, reports and Splunk AI Toolkit (MLTK) machine-learning pipelines — grounded in your running Splunk (your knowledge objects, live command syntax, CIM models), run for real before they are saved, owned by the calling user. The depth is the difference. Where a generic MCP-only assistant talks to Splunk through one broad door, Adjutant AI ships fine-grained, Splunk-aware tools across Core, Enterprise Security, ITSI, TrackMe, ServiceNow and the AI Toolkit, each scoped to one job and run under your existing Splunk ACLs. Extend it with HTTP tools or any MCP server. New in 2.1 — a fraud capability that starts by telling you what you cannot yet detect. The Fraud Data Coverage Audit grades your estate against nine use cases (including AML) and returns ready, partial or blocked with the specific blocker, identifying event families by what events contain rather than by sourcetype name. Entity resolution runs before scoring, because risk accumulates per entity. Generated rules are weighted contributions with readable reasons, emitted into Enterprise Security's risk framework where it exists and into RBA's own field vocabulary where it does not. Nothing generated is ever enabled or scheduled. New in 2.0 — ITSI Root Cause Analysis with no LLM in the answer. It walks your real dependency graph, verifies the data behind every KPI, scores the evidence transparently, then lets an LLM narrate. The same evidence always gives the same answer. A red KPI on a dead feed is a data problem, and it names the forwarder, HEC, DB Connect, Cribl or Edge Processor leg at fault. Plus durable memory, scheduled playbooks, governed integrations, and per-tenant resource-consumption reporting. Your SOC can watch the agent: LLM calls, tool and ServiceNow calls, config changes, unattended verdicts and policy refusals emitted as OCSF events to an index Enterprise Security already watches. On-prem, no cloud egress, off by default. Bring your own LLM: Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Groq, Gemini, Bedrock, Ollama (fully offline) or OpenRouter — server-side, so keys never leave the search head. Multi-tenant by design. Free, Professional, Enterprise and MSP tiers, self-serve and air-gap-friendly.

Description:
MCP Server for Splunk Platform The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard and framework that enables seamless, secure, and standardized two-way communication between AI applications (like large language models) and external data sources or tools. Splunk's Model Context Protocol (MCP) server leverages this to provide a standardized, secure, and scalable interface to connect AI assistants, agents, and other intelligent systems with data in the Splunk platform for both Enterprise & Cloud customers in beta. 🔑 Key Features - Universal Connectivity Seamlessly connects AI agents and tools to Splunk data resources in a secure and efficient manner. - Enterprise-Grade Security Includes built-in authentication, authorization, and Role-Based Access Control (RBAC). - Rapid Deployment Offers a plug-and-play solution, eliminating the need for custom integrations. ⚙️ Core Capabilities - Explore the Data Navigate and interact with Splunk data effortlessly. - Discover Knowledge Objects Identify and access relevant saved searches, lookups, and other knowledge assets. - Execute Searches Run powerful Splunk queries to extract insights and drive intelligent workflows. - Leverage AI capabilities from Splunk’s AI Assistant for SPL & MLTK SPL search generation from natural language, search optimization, search explanation, retrieve MLTK models and algorithms.

**TrackMe 2.4.12 — Topology Studio opens to Foundation Edition, with critical stability hardening for large logical-group deployments.** * **Topology Studio is now open to Foundation Edition.** The feature was introduced in TrackMe 2.4.9 but was mistakenly restricted to Enterprise and Unlimited customers. Foundation customers can now use the complete authoring experience and manage Topology Alerts. Existing security boundaries and the normal licence read-only state are unchanged. * **Critical memory-stability fix for large logical-group deployments.** In versions 2.4.6 through 2.4.11, logical-group processing could trigger a repeating cycle of overlapping background refreshes. At scale, this could put severe memory pressure on `splunkd` and cause an out-of-memory termination. TrackMe 2.4.12 prevents the cycle and limits duplicate refresh work while retaining automatic updates. Customers with large numbers of logical groups should treat this as a critical upgrade and prioritise deployment of 2.4.12. * **No external machine-learning application dependency.** TrackMe no longer requires the Splunk Machine Learning Toolkit or the Splunk Scientific Python add-on because outlier detection runs on TrackMe’s native engine. Outdated checks for those applications could report missing requirements and interfere with Virtual Tenant creation when they were absent; the checks are now removed. * **Incremental outlier baselines.** Supported native KV Store models can retain representative historical observations within a configured bound across training cycles. Full retraining remains the default; incremental learning can be inherited from the system setting or selected per model, and switching back to full performs the established full refit. * **Median and better guidance for outlier analysis.** Median is available as an outlier calculation method, making models less sensitive to occasional volume spikes than an average. The Outliers page now includes an accessible visual explanation of learning, detection, qualification and impact-based scoring, and its settings guidance reflects the shipped defaults. * **More expressive and securely shared Topology Studio views.** Authors can select a saved link, inspect its source and target, edit its label, choose one-way, bidirectional or hidden arrows, reverse a one-way relationship and decide which relationships carry impact propagation. Bidirectional links carry impact in both directions immediately. The two-step connection workflow is also more prominent and easier to follow. Tenant visibility is enforced consistently when opening saved views, previewing their history and creating or importing portable archives. * **More precise aggregates and propagation.** An aggregate can optionally be constrained to an exact subset of the entities matching its scope and filter. Generated members, live status, alerts and rendered emails all use the same membership. Red, orange and informational blue states propagate consistently, aggregate-member arrows remain visible, and member KPI choices reflect the generated entity set. * **Complete policy and coverage results at scale.** Priority, tag and SLA policies based on SPL searches or lookups now evaluate the complete result set instead of stopping at 50,000 rows. Exceptionally large policy sources stop explicitly before partial results can be applied. Host and data-source coverage analysis and expected-entity injection now read the complete tracked inventory, expose duplicate reference rows separately and fail clearly if that complete inventory cannot be loaded. * **Median volume KPIs for DSM and DHM.** The median five-minute event count is available in Performance Metrics, stateful-alert charts and ML Outliers KPI selection. Existing defaults are unchanged and history starts after upgrade; earlier values are not backfilled. * **Cleaner fresh installations.** Hybrid tracker creation now tolerates the short configuration-refresh window that can follow creation of a search macro. A deployment with no AI provider or no Virtual Tenant configured also no longer records a misleading error for that normal state. * **Dependency maintenance.** Third-party JavaScript dependencies were refreshed for the release cycle, with no known vulnerabilities reported by the release audit.
